headline: An old report that Meta is paying for seven gas plants to power its Louisiana data center resurfaced with a new date.
score_reason: Pool 6 lowered by 2: the Bloomberg story is from 27 Mar 2026 and the latest regulator step from April; nothing new on 3 Oct.
importance_line: Louisiana households could end up sharing the cost of ten gas plants built for one Meta data center, but the state commission has not yet taken its final vote and the item carries no new facts.
summary: Bloomberg reported on 27 Mar 2026 that Meta agreed to fund seven new gas-fired power plants for its planned $27 billion data center in Richland Parish, Louisiana, a story EnergyNow re-posted on 3 Oct with no new facts; KALB later reported that Entergy, the state's main utility, asked regulators to fast-track approval of the seven plants, on top of three already approved, with a final vote due in November 2026. Consumer advocates warn that part of the cost could be shifted onto other Entergy customers.
